work: Enarratio in Epistolam II B. Pauli ad Timotheum
source: Dionysii Cartusiani Opera Omnia, t. XIII (Montreuil)

1.title: EXPOSITIO CAPITULI PRIMI : PAULUS APOSTOLUS JESU CHRISTI PER VOLUNTATEM DEI.
1.title_en: Exposition of the first chapter: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God.

paras.t: PAULUS apostolus Jesu Christi per voluntatem Dei, id est Deo agente, secundum promissionem vitæ, id est propter præmium, vel ad obtinendam remunerationem vitæ quæ est in Christo Jesu, id est vitæ æternæ, quæ a Christo confertur, et in Christo consistit sicut in objecto: quæ vita est præmium, propter quod factus sum apostolus, non ab homine, sed a Deo: mandat et scribit Timotheo carissimo filio suo spirituali. Gratia gratum faciens, misericordia, id est peccatorum remissio, et pax, id est tranquillitas mentis, sit tibi a Deo Patre et Christo Jesu filio ejus Domino nostro.
paras.en: [[1:1|Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ, by the will of God|PAULUS apostolus Jesu Christi per voluntatem Dei]], that is, by God's doing, [[1:1|according to the promise of life|secundum promissionem vitæ]], that is, for the sake of the reward, or to obtain the recompense of the life [[1:1|which is in Christ Jesus|quæ est in Christo Jesu]], that is, of life everlasting, which is bestowed by Christ and consists in Christ as in its object: which life is the reward for whose sake I was made an apostle, not by man but by God: commands and writes [[1:2|To Timothy, my dearly beloved son|Timotheo carissimo filio]], his spiritual son. [[1:2|Grace|Gratia]] that makes pleasing [*gratia gratum faciens*, sanctifying grace, which makes the soul pleasing to God], [[1:2|mercy|misericordia]], that is, the remission of sins, [[1:2|and peace|et pax]], that is, tranquillity of mind, be to thee [[1:2|from God the Father and from Christ Jesus|a Deo Patre et Christo Jesu]] his Son, [[1:2|our Lord|Domino nostro]].

paras.t: Gratias ago Deo meo, cui servio a progenitoribus meis, id est exemplo antiquorum patrum meorum, videlicet Abrahæ, Isaac et Jacob, quorum vestigia imitor unum verum Deum colendo, in conscientia pura, id est sine remorsu alicujus peccati. Inde autem gratias ago, quod sine intermissione, id est omni congruo tempore, habeam tui memoriam in orationibus meis fusis pro te et aliis, nocte ac die;
paras.en: [[1:3|I give thanks to God|Gratias ago Deo meo]] [Denis reads *Deo meo*, "to my God"], [[1:3|whom I serve from my forefathers|cui servio a progenitoribus meis]], that is, after the example of my fathers of old, namely Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, in whose footsteps I follow by worshipping the one true God, [[1:3|with a pure conscience|in conscientia pura]], that is, without remorse for any sin. And I give thanks for this, [[1:3|that without ceasing|quod sine intermissione]], that is, at every fitting time, [[1:3|I have a remembrance of thee in my prayers|habeam tui memoriam in orationibus meis]] poured out for thee and for others, [[1:3|night and day|nocte ac die]];

paras.t: desiderans te videre, memor lacrymarum, quas deduxerunt oculi tui quando recessi a te, qui libentissime mecum transisses ac permansisses, ut gaudio implear, id est, ut te in bonis confirmem, et accendam ad martyrii palmam, quo facto, de tuo profectu plene exsultem; recordationem accipiens ejus fidei quæ est in te non ficta, id est tuæ veræ fidei reminiscens, quæ non est simulata, sed pura et efficax; quæ fides et habitavit, id est, firmiter fuit, primum in avia tua Loide, id est matre matris tuæ sic dicta; habitavit quoque et in matre tua Eunice. Parentum fidem commemorat, ut fidem filii roboret. Tacet vero de patre Timothei, quoniam gentilis erat et infidelis, ut dicitur. Certus sum autem quod et in te habitet fides ista.
paras.en: [[1:4|Desiring to see thee|desiderans te videre]], [[1:4|being mindful of thy tears|memor lacrymarum]], which thine eyes shed[[Jer 9:18||]] [the margin gives Jer. xx, 12, which does not fit; the phrase recalls Jer 9:18, "let our eyes shed tears"] when I went away from thee, thou who wouldst most gladly have gone along with me and stayed with me; [[1:4|that I may be filled with joy|ut gaudio implear]], that is, that I may confirm thee in good things and kindle thee toward the palm of martyrdom, and, that done, may rejoice fully in thy progress; [[1:5|Calling to mind that faith which is in thee unfeigned|recordationem accipiens ejus fidei quæ est in te non ficta]], that is, remembering thy true faith, which is not feigned but pure and effective; [[1:5|which also dwelt|quæ fides et habitavit]], that is, was firmly, [[1:5|first in thy grandmother Lois|primum in avia tua Loide]], that is, thy mother's mother, so called; it dwelt also [[1:5|and in thy mother Eunice|et in matre tua Eunice]]. He recalls the faith of the parents to strengthen the faith of the son. But he is silent about Timothy's father, because he was a Gentile and an unbeliever, as is said[[Acts 16:1||]]. And [[1:5|I am certain that in thee also|Certus sum autem quod et in te habitet fides ista]] this faith dwells.

paras.t: Propter quam causam, videlicet, quia tam bonas genitrices habuisti, et fidelis diu fuisti, admoneo te paterne, ut resuscites, id est, reformes, perficere studeas, et ad pristinos actus extendas, gratiam Dei quæ est in te, id est gratiam episcopalem et sacramentalem tibi divinitus datam in tui ordinatione vel confirmatione, per impositionem manuum […] quæ tibi positio fuit causa gratiæ dispositiva et instrumentalis. Vel potest intelligi absolute de gratia gratificante, quia per impositionem manuum Apostolorum dabatur Spiritus Sanctus. Ex his patet, quod gratia in corde Timothei erat quasi sopita et debilitata: ideo admonet eum ut reparet gratiam pristinam, proficiendo in ea. Unde etiam quod in Apocalypsi angelo Ecclesiæ Ephesi dicitur, Scio opera tua et laborem et patientiam; et post pauca, Sed habeo adversum te, quod caritatem tuam primam reliquisti; memor esto itaque unde exciderit, et age pœnitentiam, et prima opera fac: quidam exponunt de Timotheo, quem constat fuisse Ephesiorum angelum, id est episcopum.
paras.en: [[1:6|For which cause|Propter quam causam]], namely, because thou hadst such good mothers [*genitrices*: his mother and grandmother] and hast long been faithful, [[1:6|I admonish thee|admoneo te]] as a father, [[1:6|that thou stir up|ut resuscites]], that is, renew, strive to perfect, and stretch out to its former acts, [[1:6|the grace of God which is in thee|gratiam Dei quæ est in te]], that is, the episcopal and sacramental grace given thee by God in thy ordination or confirmation, [[1:6|by the imposition of my hands|per impositionem manuum]] […]; which imposition was for thee a disposing and instrumental cause of grace. Or it may be understood simply of sanctifying grace [*gratia gratificans*, the grace that makes the soul pleasing to God], because by the imposition of the hands of the Apostles the Holy Ghost was given[[Acts 8:17||]]. From this it is plain that grace in Timothy's heart was as it were asleep and weakened: therefore he admonishes him to repair his former grace by making progress in it. Hence also what is said in the Apocalypse to the angel of the Church of Ephesus, [[Apoc 2:2|I know thy works and thy labour and thy patience|Scio opera tua et laborem et patientiam]]; and a little after, [[Apoc 2:4|But I have somewhat against thee, because thou hast left thy first charity|Sed habeo adversum te, quod caritatem tuam primam reliquisti]]; [[Apoc 2:5|Be mindful therefore from whence thou art fallen: and do penance and do the first works|memor esto itaque unde exciderit, et age pœnitentiam, et prima opera fac]]: some expound of Timothy, who is known to have been the angel, that is, the bishop, of the Ephesians.

paras.t: Non enim dedit nobis Deus spiritum, id est donum, timoris pure servilis; vel, Spiritum timoris, id est animam inordinate timentem temporalia mala, videlicet eos qui corpus occidunt; sed dedit nobis spiritum, id est donum et gratiam, virtutis, id est fortitudinis contra adversa, quæ est unum de septem donis Spiritus Sancti, et dilectionis Dei ac proximi, et sobrietatis, id est temperantiæ vel discretionis. Verba hæc plenius exposita sunt ad Romanos, ubi legitur, Non accepistis spiritum servitutis iterum in timore.
paras.en: [[1:7|For God hath not given us the spirit|Non enim dedit nobis Deus spiritum]], that is, the gift, [[1:7|of fear|timoris]] that is purely servile [servile fear: fear of punishment alone, as against the filial fear of offending God]; or, *the spirit of fear*, that is, a soul that inordinately fears temporal evils, namely [[Matt 10:28|them that kill the body|eos qui corpus occidunt]]; [[1:7|but|sed]] he hath given us the spirit, that is, the gift and grace, [[1:7|of power|virtutis]], that is, of fortitude against adversities, which is one of the seven gifts of the Holy Ghost, [[1:7|and of love|et dilectionis]] of God and of neighbour, [[1:7|and of sobriety|et sobrietatis]], that is, of temperance or discretion. These words are more fully expounded on the Epistle to the Romans, where we read, [[Rom 8:15|you have not received the spirit of bondage again in fear|Non accepistis spiritum servitutis iterum in timore]].

paras.t: Noli itaque erubescere, id est, quoniam dedit nobis Deus spiritum dilectionis, non erubescas testimonium Domini nostri Jesu Christi, id est protestationem, prædicationem seu confessionem Christi; sed sine rubore et confusione testare coram hominibus, quod Christus sit Deus et homo, qui sua passione universum mundum redemit, resurrexit, cœlos ascendit. Unde ait Salvator in Evangelio: Qui me confessus fuerit coram hominibus, confitebor et ego eum coram Patre meo; et rursus, Qui me erubuerit et meos sermones, hunc Filius hominis erubescet. Neque erubescas me vinctum ejus, id est me Paulum pro fide nunc captum atque ligatum.
paras.en: [[1:8|Be not thou therefore ashamed|Noli itaque erubescere]]: that is, since God hath given us the spirit of love, be not ashamed [[1:8|of the testimony of our Lord|testimonium Domini nostri]] Jesus Christ, that is, of the witness, preaching or confession of Christ; but without blushing or confusion bear witness before men that Christ is God and man, who by his passion redeemed the whole world, rose again, and ascended into heaven. Hence the Saviour says in the Gospel: [[Matt 10:32|that shall confess me before men, I will also confess him before my Father|Qui me confessus fuerit coram hominibus, confitebor et ego eum coram Patre meo]]; and again, [[Luke 9:26|he that shall be ashamed of me and of my words, of him the Son of man shall be ashamed|Qui me erubuerit et meos sermones, hunc Filius hominis erubescet]]. Nor be ashamed [[1:8|of me his prisoner|me vinctum ejus]], that is, of me, Paul, now taken and bound for the faith.

paras.t: Sed collabora Evangelio, id est, cum me et ceteris evangelizantibus, labora ad promulgationem ac venerationem evangelicæ legis, fortiter prædicando, juste vivendo, et pro fidei veritate mortem sustinendo, secundum virtutem Dei, id est secundum virtutem et gratiam tibi divinitus datam; qui nos liberavit per propriam passionem a jugo diaboli et pœna inferni, et vocavit ad fidem ac vitam æternam, vocatione sua sancta, id est inspiratione interna (de qua in Apocalypsi: Ego sto ad ostium et pulso), vel prædicatione evangelica quam fecit per nos: non enim nos sumus qui loquimur, sed Spiritus Patris nostri qui loquitur in nobis. Vocavit, inquam, nos, non secundum opera nostra, id est propria merita, quæ vocationem hanc nequaquam præcesserunt, sed secundum propositum suum, id est voluntatis suæ decretum seu voluntariam præordinationem, et gratiam nobis clementer infusam: quæ est effectus hujus propositi, per quem ad omnia opera meritoria promovemur atque perducimur; quæ data, id est dari præordinata, est nobis in Christo Jesu, id est per Christum, utputa per ejus incarnationem, virtutem et meritum, ante tempora sæcularia, id est ab æterno.
paras.en: But [[1:8|labour with the gospel|collabora Evangelio]], that is, labour with me and the other preachers of the gospel for the spreading and honouring of the gospel law, by preaching boldly, living justly, and suffering death for the truth of the faith, [[1:8|according to the power of God|secundum virtutem Dei]], that is, according to the power and grace given thee by God; [[1:9|Who hath delivered us|qui nos liberavit]] by his own passion from the yoke of the devil and the punishment of hell, [[1:9|and called us|et vocavit]] to faith and life everlasting, [[1:9|by his holy calling|vocatione sua sancta]], that is, by inward inspiration (of which it is said in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 3:20|I stand at the gate and knock|Ego sto ad ostium et pulso]]), or by the preaching of the gospel which he did through us: for it is not we that speak, but the Spirit of our Father that speaketh in us[[Matt 10:20||]] [Christ's words in Matt 10:20, which Denis puts in the first person]. He called us, I say, [[1:9|not according to our own works|non secundum opera nostra]], that is, our own merits, which in no way went before this calling, [[1:9|but according to his own purpose|sed secundum propositum suum]], that is, the decree of his will or his free foreordaining, [[1:9|and grace|et gratiam nobis]] mercifully poured into us: which is the effect of this purpose, by which we are moved and brought on to all meritorious works; [[1:9|which was given|quæ data]], that is, foreordained to be given, [[1:9|us in Christ Jesus|est nobis in Christo Jesu]], that is, through Christ, namely through his incarnation, power and merit, [[1:9|before the times of the world|ante tempora sæcularia]], that is, from eternity.

paras.t: Manifestata est autem, id est, publice prædicata et nota, vel evidenter impleta est, nunc tempore gratiæ, per illuminationem, id est prædicationem et doctrinam, Salvatoris nostri Jesu Christi: quam proprio ore vel per Apostolos mundo proposuit, aut certe per illuminationem factam in die Pentecostes, quando in igneis linguis Spiritus Sanctus apparens, illuminavit Apostolos ad cognoscendum et prædicandum hanc gratiam: quæ illuminatio dicitur Christi, quoniam ipse misit Spiritum Sanctum. Qui Christus sua passione destruxit, id est hominibus abstulit, mortem culpæ atque gehennæ, et corporis immortalitatem promeruit eis: quam et nunc præstat in spe, daturus eam in re quando corruptibile hoc induet incorruptionem. Hoc est quod apud Osee loquitur: De morte redimam eos; ero mors tua, o mors. Illuminavit autem, id est, notam fecit, vitam æternam, quæ est merces nostri laboris, et finis hujus peregrinationis, et incorruptionem, id est perpetuam immortalitatem, quam habebunt electi in anima et corpore post diem judicii, per Evangelium, id est Evangelii prædicationem, videlicet per se ipsum et discipulos suos, dicendo: Cognosco oves meas, et vitam æternam do eis; et alibi, Qui credit in me, non morietur in æternum. In quo Evangelio prædicando, videlicet ut id annuntiem omnibus, positus sum ego, id est a Deo ordinatus et constitutus, prædicator et apostolus et magister gentium.
paras.en: [[1:10|But is now made manifest|Manifestata est autem]], that is, publicly preached and known, or plainly fulfilled, [[1:10|now|nunc]] in the time of grace, [[1:10|by the illumination|per illuminationem]], that is, the preaching and teaching, [[1:10|of our Saviour Jesus Christ|Salvatoris nostri Jesu Christi]], which he set before the world with his own mouth or through the Apostles; or else by the illumination made on the day of Pentecost, when the Holy Ghost, appearing in tongues of fire, enlightened the Apostles to know and to preach this grace[[Acts 2:3||]] [the margin gives Acts ii, 1–4]: which illumination is called Christ's, since he himself sent the Holy Ghost[[John 16:7||]]. Christ by his passion [[1:10|hath destroyed|destruxit]], that is, took away from men, [[1:10|death|mortem]] of guilt and of hell, and merited for them the immortality of the body: which he gives even now in hope, and will give in reality when this corruptible shall put on incorruption. This is what is said in Osee: [[Osee 13:14|I will redeem them from death|De morte redimam eos]]; [[Osee 13:14|O death, I will be thy death|ero mors tua, o mors]]. [[1:10|and hath brought to light|Illuminavit autem]], that is, made known, [[1:10|life|vitam æternam]] everlasting, which is the reward of our labour and the end of this pilgrimage, [[1:10|and incorruption|et incorruptionem]], that is, everlasting immortality, which the elect will have in soul and body after the day of judgement, [[1:10|by the gospel|per Evangelium]], that is, by the preaching of the gospel, namely through himself and his disciples, saying: I know my sheep[[John 10:27||]], and [[John 10:28|I give them life everlasting|vitam æternam do eis]]; and elsewhere, He that [[John 11:26|believeth in me shall not die for ever|credit in me, non morietur in æternum]] [the margin reads Ibid. v, 26; the words are John 11:26]. [[1:11|Wherein|In quo]] gospel, that is, in preaching it, namely that I may announce it to all, [[1:11|I am appointed|positus sum ego]], that is, ordained and established by God, [[1:11|a preacher and an apostle and teacher of the Gentiles|prædicator et apostolus et magister gentium]].

paras.t: Ob quam causam etiam, videlicet propter Evangelii prædicationem, hæc, id est incarcerationem, ligationem et alia plurima, patior; sed non confundor in me ipso, quasi turpe aliquid operans: imo glorior in adversis. Verbum equidem crucis pereuntibus stultitia est; his vero qui salvi fiunt, id est nobis, virtus Dei est. Scio enim cui credidi, scilicet Deo omnipotenti, qui est via, veritas et vita, et certus sum quia potens est depositum meum, id est beatitudinem mihi paratam, quam merui et apud ipsum reposui, servare in illum diem, id est usque ad diem remunerationis meæ, hoc est usque ad diem mortis, quantum ad glorificationem animæ, et usque in diem extremi judicii, quantum ad glorificationem corporis mei.
paras.en: [[1:12|For which cause, I also|Ob quam causam etiam]], namely on account of the preaching of the gospel, [[1:12|suffer|patior]] [[1:12|these things|hæc]], that is, imprisonment, binding and very many other things; [[1:12|but I am not ashamed|sed non confundor]] in myself, as though doing something shameful: nay, I glory in adversities. For indeed [[1 Cor 1:18|the word of the cross, to them indeed that perish, is foolishness|Verbum equidem crucis pereuntibus stultitia est]]: [[1 Cor 1:18|but to them that are saved, that is, to us, it is the power of God|his vero qui salvi fiunt, id est nobis, virtus Dei est]]. [[1:12|For I know whom I have believed|Scio enim cui credidi]], namely almighty God, who is [[John 14:6|the way, and the truth, and the life|via, veritas et vita]], [[1:12|and I am certain that he is able|et certus sum quia potens est]] [[1:12|to keep|servare]] [[1:12|that which I have committed unto him|depositum meum]], that is, the beatitude prepared for me, which I have merited and laid up with him, [[1:12|against that day|in illum diem]], that is, until the day of my reward: that is, until the day of death as regards the glorification of the soul, and until the day of the last judgement as regards the glorification of my body.

paras.t: Insuper admonet Timotheum. Formam habens sanorum verborum, id est tu, Timothee, habens seriem sanctarum prædicationum, seu formam evangelicorum verborum, quæ verba a me prædicante audisti: habens, inquam, hæc verba in fide, id est cum fidei observatione, et dilectione in Christo Jesu, id est per gratiam Christi ad gloriam ejus, vel secundum voluntatem ipsius, bonum depositum custodi, id est, gratiam tibi concessam conserva, et officium tibi commissum digne prosequere. Vel sic: Bonum depositum de quo nunc dixi, id est præmium tibi apud Deum repositum pro tuo labore, custodi, ne illud per negligentiam perdas. Per Spiritum Sanctum, id est, non tuis viribus, sed adjutorio Spiritus Sancti hoc age, qui habitat in nobis per caritatem et gratiam, quoniam sumus templum Dei. Dominus enim in templo sancto suo.
paras.en: He further admonishes Timothy. [[1:13|Hold the form of sound words|Formam habens sanorum verborum]] [Denis reads *habens*, "having", for the Vulgate's *habe*, "hold"], that is, thou, Timothy, having the course of holy preachings, or the form of the gospel words, [[1:13|which thou hast heard of me|quæ verba a me prædicante audisti]] as I preached: having, I say, these words [[1:13|in faith|in fide]], that is, with the keeping of the faith, [[1:13|and in the love which is in Christ Jesus|et dilectione in Christo Jesu]], that is, through the grace of Christ unto his glory, or according to his will, [[1:14|Keep the good thing committed to thy trust|bonum depositum custodi]], that is, preserve the grace granted to thee, and carry out worthily the office entrusted to thee. Or thus: the good deposit of which I have just spoken, that is, the reward laid up for thee with God for thy labour, keep, lest thou lose it through negligence. [[1:14|by the Holy Ghost|Per Spiritum Sanctum]], that is, not by thy own strength, but do this by the help of the Holy Ghost, [[1:14|who dwelleth in us|qui habitat in nobis]] by charity and grace, since we are the temple of God[[1 Cor 3:16||]][[1 Cor 3:17||]]. For [[Ps 10:5|The Lord is in his holy temple|Dominus enim in templo sancto suo]].

paras.t: Scis hoc, id est, jam plane agnoscis, vel scire debes, quod aversi sunt a me omnes qui in Asia sunt, id est, quod universi qui nunc recesserunt a me cum perfido corde, sunt in Asia minori; ex quibus, id est de quorum numero, sunt Phigelus et Hermogenes. Hi, ut legitur, fraudulenter accesserunt Apostolum ut discerent ejus mysteria, quatenus materiam calumniandi haberent: qui quum se manifestatos conspicerent, abierunt.
paras.en: [[1:15|Thou knowest this|Scis hoc]], that is, thou now plainly recognisest it, or oughtest to know it, [[1:15|that all they who are in Asia are turned away from me|quod aversi sunt a me omnes qui in Asia sunt]], that is, that all who have now gone away from me with faithless heart are in Asia Minor; [[1:15|of whom|ex quibus]], that is, of whose number, [[1:15|are Phigellus|sunt Phigelus]] and [[1:15|Hermogenes|Hermogenes]]. These, as we read, came to the Apostle deceitfully to learn his mysteries, so that they might have matter for calumny; and when they saw themselves found out, they went away.

paras.t: Det misericordiam Dominus Onesiphori domui, id est fideli familiæ Onesiphori Asiani, quia sæpe me refrigeravit, id est, consolatus est et refocillavit, necessaria ministrando, et catenam meam, id est me catenis vinctum, non erubuit verecundando de tali magistro; sed quum Romam venisset, sollicite me quæsivit et invenit.
paras.en: [[1:16|The Lord give mercy to the house of Onesiphorus|Det misericordiam Dominus Onesiphori domui]], that is, to the faithful household of Onesiphorus of Asia, [[1:16|because he hath often refreshed me|quia sæpe me refrigeravit]], that is, comforted and revived me by supplying my needs; and [[1:16|of my chain|catenam meam]], that is, of me bound with chains, he [[1:16|hath not been ashamed|non erubuit]], blushing for such a master; [[1:17|But when he was come to Rome, he carefully sought me and found me|sed quum Romam venisset, sollicite me quæsivit et invenit]].

paras.t: Det illi Dominus Pater invenire misericordiam, id est gratiam adipisci et vitam æternam a Domino Filio: cui Pater dedit omne judicium, juxta illud: Deus, judicium tuum regi da; in illa die, id est in die mortis atque judicii. Talis modus loquendi in veteri Testamento usitatior est, ut ibi: Pluit Dominus super Sodomam ignem et sulphur a Domino. Et quanta beneficia Ephesi, id est in Epheso, ministraverit mihi Onesiphorus iste, tu melius nosti qui præsens fuisti, quam ea quæ Romæ mihi ministraverit.
paras.en: [[1:18|The Lord grant unto him|Det illi Dominus]] the Father [[1:18|to find mercy|invenire misericordiam]], that is, to obtain grace and life everlasting, [[1:18|of the Lord|a Domino Filio]] the Son, to whom the Father [[John 5:22|hath given all judgment|dedit omne judicium]], according to that saying: [[Ps 71:2|Give to the king thy judgment, O God|Deus, judicium tuum regi da]]; [[1:18|in that day|in illa die]], that is, in the day of death and of judgement. This manner of speaking [the Lord giving from the Lord] is more usual in the Old Testament, as there: [[Gen 19:24|the Lord rained upon Sodom and Gomorrha brimstone and fire from the Lord|Pluit Dominus super Sodomam ignem et sulphur a Domino]]. [[1:18|And in how many things|Et quanta beneficia]] [[1:18|at Ephesus|Ephesi]], that is, in Ephesus, [[1:18|he ministered unto me|ministraverit mihi]], this Onesiphorus, [[1:18|thou very well knowest|tu melius nosti]], who wast there, better than those which he ministered to me at Rome [Denis takes *melius*, "better", as a comparative: thou knowest his services at Ephesus better than those at Rome].
